findings.title: Local cache is set before DB write, bypassing the device limit on subsequent requests
findings.body: In tagDeviceUI, the local cache entry is set before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. When the limit is reached, CreateOrUpdateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached, but the cache key remains set. Any subsequent request for the same device within the cache TTL (29 minutes) hits the cache, returns nil without consulting the database, and the authentication succeeds even though the device was never registered and the limit is still exceeded. This makes the limit enforcement non-deterministic: the same new device is rejected on its first request but admitted on every subsequent request within 29 minutes, while also being absent from the database (so usage stats and the device list undercount it). The cache should only be populated after a successful insert/update, or failed attempts should not be cached.

findings.title: TagDevice now uses the request context, so client cancellation aborts device tagging
findings.body: Previously TagDevice was invoked from a goroutine with a fresh context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Minute), decoupling the DB write from the caller. The new implementation calls a.anonDeviceService.TagDevice(ctx, ...) directly with the incoming request context. If the HTTP request is cancelled (slow client, closed connection, timeout) before the DB write completes, ctx is cancelled and CreateOrUpdateDevice returns early without inserting the device. Anonymous devices on flaky or slow connections may therefore never be tagged even though the user authenticated. This is a regression from the previous fire-and-forget behavior.

findings.title: No test covers the new synchronous error path in Authenticate when ErrDeviceLimitReached is returned
findings.body: The PR changes Authenticate so that an error from TagDevice propagates and causes authentication to fail when errors.Is(err, anonstore.ErrDeviceLimitReached) is true. This is a significant user-visible behavior change (anonymous login now fails with an error when the limit is set and full) but is only covered at the store layer by TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit. There is no test that exercises the Anonymous.Authenticate path returning ErrDeviceLimitReached, nor any test that verifies a non-limit error from TagDevice is still logged but does not block auth. This regression-prone path needs direct coverage.

findings.title: TOCTOU race allows the device limit to be exceeded under concurrent requests
findings.body: CreateOrUpdateDevice performs CountDevices followed by a separate insert/update when s.deviceLimit > 0. The two operations are not atomic and are not wrapped in a transaction or row lock. With concurrent requests all observing count == limit-1, multiple new devices can pass the check and all be inserted, taking the actual count above the configured limit. If strict enforcement is desired, this needs to be made atomic (e.g., a conditional INSERT, a transaction with SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, or a unique-constraint-based scheme). At minimum, document that the limit is best-effort.

findings.title: updateDevice silently rejects returning devices whose updated_at is older than the expiration window
findings.body: updateDevice returns ErrDeviceLimitReached when the WHERE clause matches zero rows. This happens not only for unknown device_ids (the intended case) but also for any device whose existing row has updated_at outside the [-30d, +1m] window relative to the new request. Because cleanup only deletes devices older than 61 days, a user who has not visited for 30-61 days has an existing row that will be treated as 'not existing' and rejected when the limit is full, even though their record is still in the table. Either remove the updated_at window from the UPDATE (use only device_id = ?) so existing devices can always re-activate, or document the 30-day activity requirement explicitly.

findings.title: 30-day expiration constant is duplicated and inconsistently named across packages
findings.body: The value 30 * 24 * time.Hour is defined as anonymousDeviceExpiration in both pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go (line 16) and pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/api/api.go (line 18), and as thirtyDays in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go (line 25). All three must agree; if anyone updates one (e.g., to change the expiration window) the others will drift and the limit/enforcement/list/usage-stats queries will use different windows. Centralize this constant in a single package and import it from the other two.

findings.title: Negative device_limit is silently treated as unlimited
findings.body: MustInt64(0) returns the parsed value when it is a valid integer. A negative value (e.g., device_limit = -1) is stored as-is in cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit. The check in CreateOrUpdateDevice is `if s.deviceLimit > 0`, so a negative value disables the limit the same as 0. Operators who misconfigure the setting will believe the limit is active when it is not. Validate the value at load time and log/return an error for values < 0, or treat any value <= 0 as 'unlimited' and document it.

findings.title: updateDevice name does not reflect that it rejects new devices when the limit is reached
findings.body: The function is named updateDevice and its doc-comment says 'updates a device if it exists', but in CreateOrUpdateDevice it is also used as the path that rejects unknown device_ids when the limit is full (rowsAffected == 0 -> ErrDeviceLimitReached). Readers tracing the call site will be surprised that an 'update' function causes new-device rejections. Rename or split, and update the comment.

findings.title: untagDevice logs the wrong variable when the device delete fails
findings.body: In untagDevice the delete error is captured as errD, but the log call uses 'error', err (the post-login hook parameter, which was checked for non-nil above and is nil here). So when the DeleteDevice fails, the log message says 'Failed to untag device' with err=<nil>, providing no diagnostic value. Change the log to use errD. This is pre-existing but in a file modified by this PR and adjacent to the new error-return path.
